newsitem.title: USA: N.Dakota soil moisture levels deteriorate.
newsitem.headline: N.Dakota soil moisture levels deteriorate.

text.p: North Dakota's soil moisture conditions deteriorated below the five-year average moisture levels during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said.

"While (the dryness) has benefited small grain harvest, it detracts from late season crop yields, makes potato and sugarbeet digging more difficult and benefits grasshopper egg laying," the service said in its weekly crop progress report.
Low lying areas of the state also received the first mild frost of the season, although the extent of damage to corn and soybeans was unknown.
DNS wheat harvested 90 percent vs 83 year ago, 79 average.
Durum wheat harvested 71 percent vs 64 y/a, 63 avge.
Oats harvested 95 percent vs 85 y/a, 88 avge.
Barley harvested 97 percent vs 94 y/a, 88 avge.
Sunflower bracts turned yellow 79 pct vs 79 y/a, 67 avge.
Potatoes dug 24 percent vs 20 year ago, 31 avge.
Topsoil moisture rated 2 percent surplus, 44 adequate, 29 short and 25 very short, versus average of five surplus, 64 adequate, 24 short and seven very short.
